correctness.rationale: After the substitution x=cos(2πr/m), sampled nonnegativity is a two-variable linear program for q(x)=1+λx+c(2x²-1). For m≥4 the two sampled cosine values bracketing -1/√2 supply both an explicit feasible factorization and a positive dual combination eliminating c, so the lower and upper bounds coincide. Aliased m=2,3 are handled explicitly. The 8|m case follows from the sampled point x=-1/√2. The universal proof is independent of finite computation.

value.rationale: This is the complete exact solution of the first finite-grid Carathéodory–Fejér problem in which sampling can strictly improve the classical continuous extremal. The theorem identifies the arithmetic resonance 8|m, gives the exact gain on every other nonaliased grid, and determines the unique off-resonance extremizer by the two adjacent cosine nodes. That grid-geometry mechanism is a reusable structural fact, not a one-modulus table or a mere numerical increment.
